status_summary: A presidential memorandum of 2025-01-20 directed Commerce and USTR to review trade deficits, unfair foreign trade practices and existing trade agreements and report by 2025-04-01; it applies to all major partners and does not name the EU or UK. The US and UK announced the Economic Prosperity Deal general terms on 2025-05-08, and Executive Order 14309 (signed 2025-06-16) implemented auto, aerospace and steel and aluminum provisions. The US and EU issued a joint statement on a framework on 2025-08-21, which describes itself as a first step and uses non-binding language, and a Federal Register notice of 2025-09-25 implemented its tariff elements. The Supreme Court held on 2026-02-20 that the emergency-powers statute does not authorize tariffs; a law firm reports a 10 percent Section 122 surcharge from 2026-02-24; EU Regulation 2026/1455 applies from 2026-07-01; and a Federal Register notice (91 FR 47318) applies Section 301 duties from 2026-07-24 at 10 percent net of most-favored-nation rates for the EU and a flat 10 percent for the UK. The approach is a government-wide, tariff-driven review followed by deals, not an EU-specific review.

timeline.event: The America First Trade Policy memorandum directed Commerce and USTR to report by 2025-04-01 on the causes of persistent trade deficits, on unfair trade practices by other countries, and on revisions to existing trade agreements needed for reciprocal concessions; it does not name the EU or UK.
The US and UK announced the general terms of the Economic Prosperity Deal, per USTR's listing.

Executive Order 14309 (signed 2025-06-16, published 2025-06-23 at 90 FR 26419) implements the general terms of the US-UK Economic Prosperity Deal: a 100,000-vehicle annual quota of UK-made cars at a 10 percent combined rate, an end to certain tariffs on UK civil aircraft products, and a direction to Commerce to set tariff-rate quotas for UK steel and aluminum at a later time.

The US and EU issue a joint statement on a framework for an agreement on reciprocal, fair and balanced trade: a combined 15 percent ceiling on most EU goods, EU tariff elimination on US industrial goods, mutual acceptance of auto standards, energy and investment pledges and digital trade commitments; it calls itself a first step, uses intent language for many items and does not say it is legally binding.

A Commerce and USTR Federal Register notice (90 FR 46136, effective 2025-09-25) amends the tariff schedule to implement tariff-related elements of the US-EU framework: listed EU products and aircraft parts are exempted from reciprocal tariffs, and automobile tariffs under Proclamation 10908 are removed where the most-favored-nation rate is 15 percent or higher and otherwise reduced so the combined rate is 15 percent, with the automobile changes applying to goods entered from 2025-08-01 and the aircraft changes from 2025-09-01; the notice relies on Executive Order 14346.
The Supreme Court held 6-3 in Learning Resources v. Trump that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act does not authorize tariffs.
timeline.source: Supreme Court of the United States

timeline.event: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, adopted 2026-06-25, applies from 2026-07-01 until 2029-12-31: it sets zero EU duties on listed US-origin goods, opens tariff quotas for certain US agricultural and seafood products, and allows the Commission to suspend these concessions if the US does not implement the 2025-08-21 joint statement, with a recital referring to a 15 percent all-inclusive US tariff ceiling.

Additional duties under Section 301 apply from 2026-07-24 per the USTR Federal Register notice of 2026-07-28 (91 FR 47318), which concludes forced-labor investigations of 60 economies: the EU rate is set so the most-favored-nation duty plus the Section 301 duty equals 10 percent, and the UK faces a flat 10 percent.

title: Review US-EU trade for fairness and reciprocity; develop trade with the post-Brexit UK
